proposal: The Mandate recommends reversing the prior administration's non-enforcement of Section 117 of the Higher Education Act, which requires colleges to report foreign gifts and contracts of $250,000 or more. It calls for investigating institutions that fail to comply and referring them to the Department of Justice, and for working with Congress to tie foreign-source reporting compliance to eligibility for federal aid, particularly under Titles IV and VI.

status_summary: The executive parts are under way. Executive Order 14282 (signed 2025-04-23) directs the Education Secretary to enforce Section 117, conduct audits and investigations and seek enforcement through the Attorney General, and makes compliance a condition for federal grants; ED returned enforcement to its Office of General Counsel and opened investigations of Harvard (notice dated 2025-04-17), UC Berkeley (announced 2025-04-25) and Penn (2025-05-08), and CRS counted four investigations as of March 2026. ED opened a new reporting portal in January 2026, agreed in February 2026 that the State Department would administer reporting and civil investigations, and with State opened investigations of Duke University and the University of North Dakota in mid-September 2026 (reported as 2026-09-15). The statutory link to aid eligibility is not law: the DETERRENT Act (H.R. 1048) passed the House 241 to 169 on 2025-03-27 and was referred to the Senate HELP Committee on 2025-03-31 with no further action recorded, and no DOJ referral was found.

timeline.event: The House passed H.R. 1048, the DETERRENT Act, 241 to 169; it would lower the reporting threshold and add penalties including loss of Title IV funding.
ED's Office of the General Counsel sent Harvard University a notice of a Section 117 investigation (20 U.S.C. 1011f) with records requests due within 30 calendar days.

Executive Order 14282 was signed (published 2025-04-28), directing the Education Secretary to enforce Section 117 and hold noncompliant institutions accountable through audits, investigations and Attorney General enforcement.
ED announced that Section 117 enforcement was returning to its Office of General Counsel and opened an investigation of UC Berkeley, following a Harvard investigation announced the week before.

ED opened a Section 117 investigation of the University of Pennsylvania, citing inaccurate and untimely foreign disclosures and requesting records within 30 days (ED release undated; date from a law-firm summary).

ED's new Section 117 reporting portal was scheduled to open on this date, per an ED announcement that warns noncompliant institutions of possible DOJ enforcement; CRS confirms the portal was established in January 2026.

ED and the State Department signed an interagency agreement under which State administers biannual reporting and the portal and can start civil investigations, with ED keeping leadership of enforcement.
ED published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice to renew the foreign gifts and contracts disclosure collection through the new portal.

The Education Department, with the State Department, opened Section 117 foreign funding investigations of Duke University and the University of North Dakota, citing untimely and incomplete disclosures and requesting records within 30 days; the date is inferred from news reports (the notice to the University of North Dakota is reported as dated Tuesday 2026-09-15, and one report places the announcement on that Tuesday, another on Wednesday 2026-09-16), because the ED release and notice could not be opened.

title: Enforce HEA Section 117 foreign gift reporting, refer violators to DOJ, tie it to aid
uncertainties: The Harvard notice of 2025-04-17 was read on the FSA Partners site. The Penn release on ed.gov carries no date, so the 2025-05-08 date comes from a law-firm summary in eCampus News; the ED Berkeley release has no publication date and says only that Harvard came a week earlier, so the Berkeley event is cited to the same summary and the ED page supports its content. The ED portal announcement page carries only a last-reviewed date of 2025-12-01 and announced the 2026-01-02 opening in advance. CRS reports four investigations without naming them. The Duke and University of North Dakota investigations are dated 2026-09-15 by inference: the ED press release and the Section 117 notice to the University of North Dakota on ed.gov could not be opened this run (ed.gov refused the connection), Valley News Live (published 2026-09-16) says the agencies announced the investigations on Tuesday, and North Dakota Monitor (published 2026-09-17) says the announcement came Wednesday and the notice letter is dated Tuesday; a JNS report of 2026-09-17 also covers them. The 30-day records window would have closed around mid-October 2026, and no outcome was found. A State Department letter of 2026-07-14 to university governing boards dates the ED and State partnership to 2026-02-23, where the CRS paper gives 2026-02-20, and states that it neither announces nor waives any enforcement action. GovInfo BILLSTATUS shows H.R. 1048 passed the House 241 to 169 on 2025-03-27 and was referred to Senate HELP on 2025-03-31 with no later action, and the Senate companion S. 1296 was referred to HELP on 2025-04-03; congress.gov could not be fetched. A Federal Register search for foreign gifts since 2026-09-01 reportedly found no Section 117 rule, and no DOJ referral or civil action was found in the CRS paper or the sources read. Facts are consistent with Foreword record c00-14, which covers the same enforcement actions.
